title: A pipeline destroys an existing PIPE1.$$$ file
steps: Boot followup with multi-boot-fixture.img and followup-fixture.img. CD \T; TYPE PIPE1.$$$; TYPE ONE.TXT | SORT; DIR PIPE1.$$$; TYPE PIPE1.$$$.
observed: The sentinel USER-OWNED-PIPE-FILE is readable before the pipe. The pipe prints ALPHA, then the sentinel file is gone. The stopped-image extraction also has no PIPE1.$$$.
expected: Choose an unused temporary name and preserve existing files (tester expectation for temporary-file handling; original DOS Reference pp.132-135 describes pipes).

title: Output to a full disk silently becomes an empty file
steps: Boot re-full0 with multi-boot-fixture.img and full0-fixture.img. CD \T; DIR /W; ECHO TEST > FULL.OUT; DIR FULL.OUT; TYPE FULL.OUT.
observed: DIR reports 0 bytes free. ECHO returns without an error; FULL.OUT exists with zero bytes instead of TEST plus CR/LF. The source files remain intact.
expected: Report a disk-full write error; do not silently discard requested output (tester expectation; DOS Reference redirection pp.132-135).

title: A pipeline on a full disk silently loses its input
steps: On the same full0 fixture, CD \T; TYPE ONE.TXT | SORT; ECHO PIPE-RETURNED.
observed: The pipe prints nothing and no error. PIPE-RETURNED appears normally. ONE.TXT contains ALPHA plus CR/LF. Repeated after filling the last 512 bytes in re-full512.
expected: Print ALPHA or report failure to create/write the pipe intermediate (tester expectation; DOS Reference pp.132-135).

title: COPY reports Bad command for a disk-full write
steps: On full0-fixture.img, CD \T; COPY LONG.TXT FULL.BIN; DIR FULL.BIN.
observed: COPY prints Bad command or file name and leaves a zero-byte FULL.BIN. LONG.TXT exists and is 76800 bytes.
expected: A disk-space/write failure diagnostic identifying why COPY failed; command syntax and source are valid (tester expectation).

title: A long batch file silently stops before its final command
steps: Boot suite4 with multi-boot-fixture.img and suite-fixture.img; run \CASES\B063.BAT. It CALLs BIG.BAT, which contains BIG-BEGIN, 65 long REM lines, and BIG-END.
observed: BIG-BEGIN and the caller's BIG-RETURNED print, but BIG-END never executes; no limit/error is reported.
expected: Run the complete batch or explicitly reject it. pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:19-25 describes a batch as a sequence of commands, with no file-size restriction. Suspected cause (guess): os/milton/command.c:4212 BATCH_FILE_MAX=4096. Exact contract, pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:20-21: "InitechDOS carries out the commands in it one after another".

title: SHIFT loses arguments after the ninth
steps: Run \CASES\B060.BAT, or TEN one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven on more-fixture.img.
observed: The original ninth argument is nine. After SHIFT, %9 is empty; ten and eleven never become available.
expected: Shift later arguments into %9 (DOS Reference printed p.151, PDF236). The Initech manual explicitly limits initial arguments to nine, but this is a DOS compatibility gap.

title: SHIFT changes %0 contrary to the shipped manual
steps: Run \CASES\B060.BAT with its eleven arguments.
observed: ZERO initially identifies the batch path; after SHIFT, ZERO=one.
expected: The shipped Reference ch4-batch.tex:247 says "%0, the name of the batch file, is not changed." Actual shifting of %0 agrees with original DOS p.151; fix the manual contract rather than changing DOS-compatible behavior.

title: A path-qualified batch name requires the .BAT extension
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; A:\T\BATCH2; A:\T\BATCH2.BAT; BATCH2.
observed: The first form says Bad command or file name. Both controls print BATCH2-RAN.
expected: Resolve .BAT for a qualified name as for a bare name. pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:32 says to type the name without its extension; original DOS batch invocation uses drive/path forms. Exact wording, pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:32: "type its name without the extension".

title: COMMAND without /C cannot open a nested prompt
steps: Boot followup; type COMMAND. Then try COMMAND /C COMMAND /C ECHO NESTED.
observed: Bare COMMAND says Invalid number of parameters. Nested /C works and prints NESTED.
expected: Start a secondary command processor and allow EXIT back to the caller. pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-b.tex:102-104 promises typing commands in a second copy; DOS Reference COMMAND pp.46-47. Exact wording, pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-b.tex:102-104: "so that you can type commands without leaving the program".

title: COMMAND /C loses its child program exit status
steps: Boot advanced-misc (geometry-boot-fixture.img, more-fixture.img); CD \T; ERR0.COM; COMMAND /C ERR7.COM; IF ERRORLEVEL 7 ECHO CHILD-EXIT7; IF NOT ERRORLEVEL 7 ECHO CHILD-STATUS-LOST. Run ERR7.COM directly as a control.
observed: The /C form prints CHILD-STATUS-LOST; the direct form prints DIRECT-EXIT7. ERR7.COM exits through INT 21h/AH=4Ch with AL=7.
expected: Propagate the child status so ERRORLEVEL can test it (tester DOS command-processor expectation; Reference IF p.147 and Initech ch4-batch.tex:185-186).

title: CD drive: does not display that drive's current directory
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; CD C:\CHOME; CD D:\DHOME; CD C:; CD D:; CD.
observed: Both drive-only queries are silent; CD alone still prints A:\T. Drive-relative file access and switching drive show that per-drive directories were set.
expected: Display C:\CHOME and D:\DHOME without switching drives (DOS Reference printed p.42/PDF127).

title: ATTRIB cannot find a readable file on D:
steps: Boot advanced-driveutils; CD \T; TYPE D:\DHOME\SAME.TXT; ATTRIB D:\DHOME\SAME.TXT; ATTRIB +R D:\DHOME\SAME.TXT.
observed: TYPE prints D-DRIVE. Both ATTRIB forms print Invalid path (or file not found).
expected: Read and set attributes on the specified mounted drive. pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-a.tex:9-12 accepts a drive-qualified file. The filename syntax at pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-a.tex:11 explicitly begins with optional d: and path; line 26 says "names the files to change or display".

title: CHKDSK reports a FAT error on valid C: and D: volumes
steps: Boot advanced-driveutils using the geometry-corrected boot fixture; CHKDSK C:; CHKDSK D:. Compare ordinary DIR/TYPE/COPY operations on those volumes.
observed: Both checks say Disk error reading (or writing) FAT. The same volumes support file reads and writes. CHKDSK on A: works.
expected: Check the requested mounted FAT12 volume; do not report a disk error simply for its drive letter (DOS CHKDSK and pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-a.tex, CHKDSK).

title: TREE ignores an explicit other-drive operand
steps: Boot suite4; CD \T; CD D:\DHOME; TREE D: /F. Also TREE D:\DHOME /F in followup.
observed: TREE D: lists volume INITECH and A:\T contents. The absolute D: form says Invalid path despite the directory being readable with TYPE.
expected: Walk the specified drive/path and label that volume (pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-c.tex:125-140). The TREE syntax at pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-c.tex:127-128 includes a drive-qualified path; line 131 says "names the directory to start from".

title: LABEL rejects a valid mounted D: volume
steps: Boot suite4; VOL D:; LABEL D: NEWLABEL.
observed: VOL displays EXTRA, but LABEL returns Invalid drive specification.
expected: Honor a specified valid drive (original DOS LABEL drive syntax; tester DOS 3.3 expectation). pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-b.tex:240-242 explicitly restricts LABEL to the current drive, so this is a compatibility gap, not a broken promise in that manual.

title: FIND ignores filename operands and waits for keyboard input
steps: Boot suite2; run \CASES\B032.BAT, whose first command is FIND "Alpha" LINES.TXT. Wait 12 seconds; or run that command directly from A:\T.
observed: No search results or file header appear; FIND waits for standard input. Ctrl-Z plus Enter returns. FIND "Alpha" < LINES.TXT works.
expected: Open the named input file (DOS Reference pp.72-73/PDF157-158). Initech documentation only describes redirection; this is a compatibility gap.

title: FIND returns incorrect status for no match and malformed arguments
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; FIND "absent" < ONE.TXT; IF ERRORLEVEL 1 ECHO RC1; IF NOT ERRORLEVEL 1 ECHO RC0. Also run FIND bad < ONE.TXT; IF ERRORLEVEL 2 ECHO BAD-ARGS-RC2; IF NOT ERRORLEVEL 2 ECHO BAD-ARGS-LOW.
observed: No line matches, but RC0 is printed. The malformed form prints Invalid number of parameters but BAD-ARGS-LOW, not BAD-ARGS-RC2.
expected: Return 1 when no matching line exists, 0 when a match exists (tester DOS FIND exit-status memory; distinguish from malformed-argument status).

title: FIND stops its search string at the first embedded quote
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; FIND "He said ""yes""" < QUOTES.TXT.
observed: Both He said "yes" and He said no are printed, as if searching only for He said .
expected: Match the embedded quoted word, returning only the first line (DOS Reference pp.72-73/PDF157-158, quotation-mark handling).

title: FIND silently accepts an unknown switch
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; FIND /BAD "ALPHA" < ONE.TXT.
observed: It prints ALPHA with no invalid-switch diagnostic.
expected: Reject an unsupported switch with a useful error (tester expectation; valid switches listed on DOS p.72).

title: SORT /+n ignores the requested starting column
steps: Boot followup; CD \T; SORT /+4 < SORTCOL.TXT. The input is 01 zebra then 02 apple.
observed: The output remains 01 zebra then 02 apple.
expected: Sort apple before zebra starting at column 4 (DOS Reference printed p.116/PDF201).

title: TIME rejects hundredths of a second
steps: Boot suite3; run \CASES\B039.BAT, or TIME 13:14:15.99.
observed: Invalid time; previous time remains unchanged.
expected: Accept the .hundredths field (DOS Reference p.120/PDF205). The narrower shipped Initech syntax does not promise it; this is DOS compatibility.

title: VERIFY is unavailable
steps: Boot stock or suite3; VERIFY; VERIFY ON; VERIFY OFF.
observed: All forms say Bad command or file name.
expected: Provide the DOS write-verification switch and state query (DOS Reference p.125/PDF210). COPY /V is separately implemented.

title: ECHO. cannot emit a blank line
steps: Boot suite3; run \CASES\B036.BAT, or type ECHO. at the prompt.
observed: Bad command or file name.
expected: Output a blank line (tester DOS 3.x memory; no claim this shorthand is specified in the shipped manual).

title: ECHO OFF at the prompt prints OFF and leaves echo on
steps: Boot advanced-keyboard; ECHO OFF; ECHO; ECHO ON.
observed: OFF is printed as ordinary text; the query still says ECHO is on. The batch form does change state.
expected: Change echo state at the prompt too (tester DOS memory; DOS Reference p.143 documents ON/OFF). The Initech manual documents a separate, narrower prompt behavior.

title: Percent-delimited variables are not expanded at the prompt
steps: Boot advanced-keyboard; SET X=expanded; ECHO %X%.
observed: The output is literally %X%.
expected: Expand the environment reference to expanded (tester DOS command-line memory). Initech documentation only promises expansion in batch files, so this is compatibility, not a false manual-contract claim.

title: DIR includes hidden and system files in normal listings
steps: Boot suite2; run \CASES\B003.BAT. HIDDEN.TXT has +H and SYSTEM.TXT has +S, set by mattrib during fixture preparation.
observed: DIR /W includes HIDDEN.TXT and SYSTEM.TXT; normal and .TXT listings do too.
expected: Omit hidden/system files from ordinary DOS 3.3 DIR output (original DOS Reference DIR pp.57-58; tester attribute expectation).

title: Protected-file redirection reports Bad command
steps: Boot suite2; CD \T; ECHO LOST > READONLY.TXT; ECHO LOST >> READONLY.TXT; TYPE READONLY.TXT.
observed: Both attempts say Bad command or file name. The protected contents remain PROTECTED.
expected: Report Access denied for a protected destination (tester diagnostic expectation; pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-a.tex:227-228 uses that wording for COPY protection).

title: FDISK labels both mounted primary partitions C:
steps: Boot advanced-fdisk with geometry-boot-fixture.img; FDISK; 4; Enter.
observed: Both partition rows start C:, though the second volume is mounted and accessible as D:. The corrected CHS fixture rules out the earlier bad-cylinder display.
expected: Show C: for the first and D: for the second mapped volume (tester consistency expectation; FDISK partition display).

title: A malformed COM file halts the entire machine
steps: Boot prog-garbage using program-fixture.img; CD \T; GARBAGE.COM. Fixture bytes are 0F 0B (invalid opcode). Try ECHO ALIVE afterwards.
observed: PC LOAD LETTER / ERROR 06 appears; serial reports PANIC vec=06 and HALTED. No prompt returns.
expected: Report the program failure and recover a usable shell (tester robustness expectation for this native hobby OS; not a promise that historical real-mode DOS isolated arbitrary programs). The panic wording itself is deliberate.

title: An unsupported 16-bit MZ file halts without a screen diagnostic
steps: Boot prog-mz16 using program-fixture.img; CD \T; DOS16.EXE. The crafted 32-byte MZ header and tiny 16-bit exit body are in prepare_special.py.
observed: The screen stays on DOS16.EXE with no new prompt/message. Serial says foreign-mz: untagged 16-bit DOS .EXE and HALTED.
expected: Refuse the unsupported format visibly and return to the shell; the brief explicitly requires a loud failure rather than a hang. Executing 16-bit programs is not demanded.

title: Ctrl-C during TYPE prints non-file bytes and does not stop output
steps: Run python3 evidence/resume_driver.py controlshort. It boots geometry-boot-fixture.img plus resume-fixture.img, CD \T, TYPE HUGE.TXT, then sends Ctrl-C after HUGE LINE 00005. The fixture has 2000 ASCII-only lines (88000 bytes).
observed: The screen fills with non-text characters. The serial capture contains 14863 NUL bytes although the input contains none. Output then reaches HUGE LINE 01999 and the shell accepts ECHO AFTER-CANCEL. The original 10000-line repeat was stopped after 125 seconds, still printing at line 09233. Ctrl-S separately holds the serial byte count steady and resumes correctly.
expected: Ctrl-C should stop TYPE and return a clean prompt; no bytes absent from the file should be printed (tester cancellation expectation and the brief; Initech Reference BREAK ch2-entries-a.tex:76 documents output-time break checking).

title: XCOPY targeting D: overwrites files on A:
steps: Run resume_driver.py xcopy. From A:\T: XCOPY A:\T\ONE.TXT D:\DHOME\ /V; DIR D:\DHOME; DIR A:\DHOME; TYPE A:\DHOME\ONE.TXT; TYPE D:\DHOME\ONE.TXT. Stop QEMU and extract both volumes. For the overwrite repeat, run resume_driver.py xcopyoverwrite: MD A:\DHOME; ECHO KEEP-A > A:\DHOME\ONE.TXT; repeat XCOPY A:\T\ONE.TXT D:\DHOME\ /V.
observed: XCOPY reports 1 File(s) copied. D:\DHOME still contains only SAME.TXT. It instead creates A:\DHOME\ONE.TXT containing 41 4c 50 48 41 0d 0a (ALPHA plus CR/LF). A source qualified with D: also yields zero copies. The stopped-image mcopy return codes are 0 for the A: file and 1 (not found) for the D: file. In the repeat, the unrelated A: sentinel changes from KEEP-A to ALPHA while no requested D: copy appears.
expected: Resolve source and destination drive letters independently and write only to the requested destination (DOS XCOPY; pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-c.tex:216-229 accepts drive-qualified source and target). Exact target contract, pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-c.tex:225: "The second names the target."

title: Invoking a batch without CALL returns to the caller anyway
steps: Run resume_driver.py batch. From A:\T run CHAIN.BAT; it prints BEFORE, invokes \CASES\CHILD.BAT arg without CALL, then has ECHO SHOULD-NOT-RETURN.
observed: CHILD=arg is followed by SHOULD-NOT-RETURN. The older followup run likewise prints CHAIN-AFTER.
expected: A plain batch invocation transfers control; only CALL resumes the caller (DOS Reference CALL p.142/PDF227).

title: Ctrl-C ends a batch without the DOS termination question
steps: Run resume_driver.py batch; \CASES\BREAK.BAT waits at PAUSE. Press Ctrl-C. Repeat with LOOP.BAT, which repeatedly uses ECHO and GOTO.
observed: Both immediately return to the DOS prompt after ^C. There is no Terminate batch job (Y/N)? and no option to continue. The PAUSE remainder is not executed.
expected: Ask Terminate batch job (Y/N)? and allow N to continue (DOS Reference p.149/PDF234). pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:38-39 documents immediate cancellation, so this is an explicit compatibility gap.

title: DEL directory refuses the documented delete-all-files form
steps: Boot suite2; run \CASES\B023.BAT: MD DELDIR; COPY ONE.TXT DELDIR\ONE.TXT; DEL DELDIR; DIR DELDIR.
observed: DEL reports Access denied; ONE.TXT remains in the directory.
expected: Treat the directory name as its contained files and apply the delete-all confirmation, leaving the directory itself (DOS Reference p.56/PDF141 explicitly says to give a directory name to delete its files).

title: DATE without an argument does not offer date entry
steps: Boot suite3; run \CASES\B038.BAT or type DATE.
observed: Only Current date is ... is displayed; execution proceeds to the next command. Startup without AUTOEXEC does have the date question.
expected: Offer Enter new date (mm-dd-yy): and let Enter retain it (DOS Reference p.55/PDF140). The Initech manual describes its display-only behavior, so this is compatibility.

title: TIME without an argument does not offer time entry
steps: Boot suite3; run \CASES\B039.BAT or type TIME.
observed: Only Current time is ... is displayed; the shell continues without an entry question. Startup without AUTOEXEC does have a time prompt.
expected: Prompt for a new time when no argument is supplied (DOS Reference p.121/PDF206). The Initech manual describes display-only TIME; this is compatibility.

title: F3 recalls the line that Ctrl-C cancelled
steps: Run resume_driver.py keyboard. ECHO TEMPLATE; then type ECHO CANCELED without Enter. Press Ctrl-C, then F3, Enter.
observed: F3 restores ECHO CANCELED and executes it, replacing the preceding completed template.
expected: Discard the cancelled line and keep the last completed command as the template. pubs/manuals/initechdos-users-guide/ch8-keys.tex:25 says "The completed line becomes the template"; lines 32-33 say InitechDOS "discards" the cancelled line. The earlier completed template is ECHO XEMPLATE in the full replay.

title: MORE pauses without displaying --More--
steps: Run resume_driver.py external. MORE < PAGES.TXT; wait; press Enter; wait; press Ctrl-C. PAGES.TXT has 65 numbered CR/LF lines.
observed: The first pause is after PAGE LINE 023, the second after 047. Both are silent, with no --More-- indicator. The serial byte count stays fixed while paused. Ctrl-C returns to the shell.
expected: Show --More-- at a page break (DOS Reference p.20/PDF105 explicitly describes the bottom-of-screen indicator).

title: The shipped 123.EXE and WORD.EXE cannot run from DOS
steps: Run resume_driver.py app123 and appword in separate sessions. CD \APPS; DIR 123.EXE; 123.EXE; A:\APPS\123.EXE. Repeat with WORD.EXE.
observed: Both present native InitechMZ files are rejected with Bad command or file name. DIR and stopped-image extraction prove the files exist (64892 and 52472 bytes). The prompt survives. SAMIR.COM, the 65536-byte native COM and the small exit programs run.
expected: Run the shipped applications from their explicit DOS paths, or give an accurate unsupported/memory diagnostic (the brief's Programs test and tester workstation expectation). This concerns the supplied native applications, separately from the foreign 16-bit MZ refusal in L030.

title: FORMAT /S cannot transfer the system from the supplied boot volume
steps: Run resume_driver.py format: FORMAT D: /S; DIR D:\. The boot volume C: is the supplied tracer image partition, with IO.SYS and INITDOS.SYS.
observed: FORMAT immediately reports Insufficient memory for system transfer. The D: contents remain intact. The source C: root has no COMMAND.COM file. Ordinary FORMAT D: followed by SYS D: succeeds when the target root entries are free.
expected: Provide a usable shipped /S installation path or accurately identify the missing source file. pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-b.tex:207-209 promises that /S "copies the system files and COMMAND.COM from drive C" and the result can start the system. Missing COMMAND.COM is a suspected cause, not a proven exclusive cause.

title: A write after FORMAT and SYS corrupts the transferred system files
steps: Run resume_driver.py syswrite. FORMAT D:; answer EXTRA, Y. SYS D:; DIR D:\; ECHO NEW-DATA > D:\NEW.TXT; TYPE D:\NEW.TXT; DIR D:\. Stop QEMU and extract D: from byte 2097152 of resume-syswrite-boot.img.
observed: SYS reports System transferred. DIR lists IO.SYS=1647 and INITDOS.SYS=196608 but claims 1456640 bytes free, already wrong. After the ten-byte NEW.TXT write, mcopy can recover only 512 bytes of IO.SYS; INITDOS.SYS cannot be read. fsck.fat -n reports a free cluster in INITDOS.SYS and shortened chains. A separate control stopped after SYS has both files byte-identical to the original C: files and 1259008 bytes free. No error is shown by the guest.
expected: Keep filesystem allocation state coherent after raw disk utilities; later ordinary writes must preserve the installed system files (tester filesystem correctness expectation; InitechDOS SYS contract ch2-entries-c.tex:74-77). Stale mounted FAT state is a root-cause guess; corruption is established by the extracted bytes and independent checker.

title: Ctrl-C advances DIR /P instead of cancelling the listing
steps: Run resume_driver.py gaps2. DIR \MANY /P; at the first Press any key to continue prompt, press Ctrl-C. Continue with Space until all 300 files are listed.
observed: Ctrl-C advances to the next page and another pause. The listing runs through F299.TXT. A final Ctrl-C at the shell only clears surplus queued spaces.
expected: Abort the active command on Ctrl-C (DOS editing-keys Reference p.159/PDF244; tester DIR expectation).

title: SORT silently accepts an unknown switch
steps: Run resume_driver.py external: SORT /BAD < LINES.TXT; IF NOT ERRORLEVEL 1 ECHO SORT-RC0.
observed: It sorts normally and prints SORT-RC0; no invalid-switch diagnostic appears.
expected: Reject unknown switches so mistyped options are visible (tester diagnostic expectation; DOS Reference p.116 lists /R and /+n).

title: An undefined batch environment variable is left as literal text
steps: Run resume_driver.py keyboard on a fresh fixture where TEST is unset; run BENV.BAT, which contains ECHO VALUE=%TEST%. As a control, resume_driver.py batch sets TEST=VALUE first.
observed: The unset case prints VALUE=%TEST%; the defined case prints VALUE=VALUE.
expected: Expand an undefined environment variable to the empty string (tester DOS batch-expansion memory). Preserve the ordinary literal-percent escape %% separately, which passes here.

title: BREAK INVALID is treated as a state query
steps: Run resume_driver.py gaps2: BREAK OFF; BREAK; BREAK ON; BREAK; BREAK INVALID.
observed: Valid ON/OFF forms work. INVALID produces BREAK is on rather than an argument error.
expected: Reject unsupported settings (tester command-diagnostic expectation; DOS BREAK syntax allows ON/OFF or no operand).

title: PROMPT $V prints V instead of the DOS version
steps: Run resume_driver.py promptversion; type PROMPT $V$G.
observed: The prompt becomes V>, rather than showing the version number.
expected: Expand $V to the version number (original DOS Reference printed p.101/PDF186, Special prompts table). The shipped Initech prompt table omits this DOS code, so this is compatibility.
